title: Clas
summary: A single-page website, written in plain JavaScript at fourteen.
paragraphs: Clas gave a small website the feel of an application: click a section and the old panel fades into the next. The original project also came with two tutorials explaining how it worked.
The restored demo keeps its early-web character, with repaired navigation and a contact form that stays inside the exhibit.
dateNote: The original Git history begins on 5 November 2012.

title: Sympl.css
summary: A responsive CSS starting point that later powered Webstiles.
paragraphs: Sympl bundled a small responsive grid and typography defaults into a stylesheet. It was a way to start a page quickly while keeping control of the HTML and CSS.
The original stylesheet survives. The accompanying demo page was recreated in 2026 to make its grid and type easy to explore.
dateNote: The original Git history begins on 6 November 2012.

title: Webstiles
summary: A way to sketch a website’s visual language directly in the browser.
paragraphs: Webstiles brought colors, typography and interface elements together in a browser-based design sheet. It helped clients compare directions before a full website was built.
The early portfolio describes Webstiles as part of the client workflow and records that its responsive template was built on Sympl.
dateNote: January 2013 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.

title: Windows 95, in CSS
summary: Four colored squares recreate a familiar piece of computing history.
paragraphs: A small animation study based on the Windows 95 launch commercial, built with CSS. The whole composition starts with the four colors of the Windows flag.
The restored version preserves the animation and adds pause and reduced-motion controls.
dateNote: The original Git history begins on 4 June 2013.

title: MusiCose
summary: A sideways-scrolling website for a fictional band from Mars.
paragraphs: A sideways-scrolling website for a fictional band from Mars.
The original files were recovered from Cloudnommy and restored as a static demo. Keyboard navigation moves between the colorful full-screen panels. The fictional contact controls are disabled.
dateNote: Surviving source files carry October 2013 timestamps; the original launch date is not established.

title: MinSlide
summary: An early JavaScript experiment in moving from one image to the next.
paragraphs: An early JavaScript experiment in moving from one image to the next.

The original files were recovered from Cloudnommy and restored as a static demo. The externally hosted photos were missing, so the restored demo identifies its solid-color substitutes. Slide controls and autoplay work again.
dateNote: Surviving source files carry October 2013 timestamps; the original launch date is not established.

title: KeyZen
summary: A typing game with a pastel keyboard and a very practical motivation.
paragraphs: KeyZen grew out of an obsession with typing faster. It turns practice into a small game, with an animated keyboard showing each key.
The existing portfolio records that it was built in a few hours for a hackathon and won first prize.
dateNote: October 2013 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.

title: The freelance years begin
summary: An early portfolio introduces a teenage designer already working on MakeUseOf.
paragraphs: The surviving homepage opens with “Hello, I’m Namanyay Goel” and describes a freelance designer and front-end developer. Its work section includes MakeUseOf, MakeUseOf TV, a music website and Webstiles.

There is already a considered client process: ask questions, make a first draft, gather feedback, then deliver the finished site. Webstiles appears both as a project and as a tool used during that process.

The page’s HTML survives, but its linked stylesheet and project thumbnails were not found. The excerpt below is presented as an archival transcription, rather than a reconstruction of the missing design.
dateNote: The page’s supporting files are dated October 2013; its surviving HTML was last modified on 9 January 2014.
excerpt: Hello, I’m Namanyay Goel, a freelance designer & front end developer. I also work at MakeUseOf as their UI designer/front end developer.

title: Agrobot & Cropstor
summary: Two agricultural product concepts, complete with interfaces, branding and motion.
paragraphs: Agrobot presented a sensor-based irrigation system with moisture tracking. Cropstor approached the other end of the process with a warehouse interface for recording farmers and their produce.
The JAD project brought the two ideas into one visual world. Product pages, phone mockups, interface screens and short videos survive from the competition work.
dateNote: The surviving product pages and assets are timestamped 1 August 2014. This dates the recovered edition, not a verified public launch.
videoCaption: Original project motion study, preserved from the 2014 files.

title: Code Warriors
summary: A website for the technology club at DPS Vasant Kunj.
paragraphs: “Hello world. We’re the Code Warriors.” The club homepage brought a school technology community onto the web, with a design built around its projects and competitions.
The surviving edition announces Code Wars 2014. This exhibit preserves the homepage design; student records and registration systems are not part of the archive.
dateNote: The page itself names Code Wars 2014; the recovered files are dated November 2014.

title: Google Code-in & FOSSASIA
summary: An early open-source notebook of utilities, tests and tutorials.
paragraphs: The Code-in collection moves between practical tools and explanations of how the web works. It includes an angle converter, a JSON validator, a wallpaper, and writing about Jekyll, automated testing and p5.js.
Other tutorials document moving a MediaWiki installation and working on web infrastructure. Together they capture the shift from building individual pages to understanding the systems behind them.
dateNote: The surviving repository runs from 8 December 2014 to 17 January 2015.
gallery: An original LXDE wallpaper from the Code-in collection.

title: Physics, made visible
summary: Interactive simulations for ideas that are easier to understand when they move.
paragraphs: A collection of browser experiments turns physics coursework into something that can be manipulated and observed. The collection includes oscillation, collisions and electrical behavior.
The original simulations remain accessible from the Physics collection.
dateNote: February 2015 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.

title: Karya
summary: Three things to do today, with enough room to actually do them.
paragraphs: Karya asks for three priorities in the morning and a check-in at night. Its original interface deliberately keeps the list short so that choosing what matters is part of the task.
The recovered app includes task views and an account system. The small version below revisits the original three-item interaction and stores your list only in this browser.
dateNote: The first surviving commit is dated 11 May 2015; the last is from November 2015.

title: Libo
summary: A household-budgeting concept with a complete mobile design.
paragraphs: Libo’s homepage presents an app to make household budgeting easier. Its interface includes an expenditure overview, an add-expense flow and a record of spending.
The recovered project includes the landing page, an interactive phone layout and several original splash screens. The screens below preserve the competition-era design.
dateNote: The repository records work on 27–28 August 2015.

title: Digital India
summary: A mobile app mockup made for C.O.R.E.
paragraphs: The Digital India concept packages news and program information into a mobile interface. Its surviving page includes the original screen compositions and names the C.O.R.E. event.
This is a visual record of the app mockup, with the original design preserved in the screenshot.
dateNote: The HTML, stylesheet and images carry 27 October 2015 timestamps.

title: Bulls & Cows
summary: A puzzle, an optimal strategy and a research paper written in 48 hours.
paragraphs: For the C.O.R.E. hackathon, Aditya and I studied the number-guessing game Bulls & Cows and the algorithms used to solve it. The work became a research paper and a JavaScript demonstration.
The existing portfolio records a first-place finish and describes this as our first experience using LaTeX.
dateNote: November 2015 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.

title: Unexpend
summary: A shopping search engine built to compare prices across stores.
paragraphs: Unexpend brought product search and comparison into one interface. The surviving code includes result templates, caching, and parsers for Amazon and Flipkart.
Its original cover artwork survives below. The historic shopping APIs and price data are not connected to this exhibit.
dateNote: The surviving Git history begins on 23 June 2016 and continues into August 2016.

title: PlayTogether
summary: A shared YouTube player for watching the same thing at the same time.
paragraphs: PlayTogether takes a YouTube link and shares playback actions through Socket.IO. Its first day of commits already includes fixes for playing multiple videos and resetting the player.
The surviving interface is a compact prototype: paste a link, start a room, and keep the players in sync. This archive preserves its interface and idea; it does not reconnect the old room server.
dateNote: The surviving repository contains four commits from 1 October 2016.

title: DubMaps
summary: The University of Washington campus, mapped through classes and events.
paragraphs: DubMaps was built around a realtime map of UW, with active classes and scheduled events attached to buildings. The source includes building locations, class schedules and event information.
The building plot below is newly drawn from the original coordinates. It preserves the geography of the project without publishing student-related datasets or presenting a 2016 timetable as current.
dateNote: The repository begins on 15 October 2016 and continues through 17 October 2016.

title: Less Confusing C++
summary: A free programming book written to make school coursework easier to follow.
paragraphs: Less Confusing C++ reorganizes introductory C++ material for high-school students. It grew out of wanting a clearer route through the course than the available study material provided.
The manuscript and exports were already preserved in Dropbox. The book remains part of the archive through its existing publication.
dateNote: June 2017 is the publication date recorded in the existing portfolio, rather than a verified manuscript start date.

title: A portfolio in motion
summary: The portfolio grows into a full visual presentation of client work.
paragraphs: The 2018 edition introduces a web and blockchain consultant. Project mockups, rich backgrounds and animated transitions make the work itself the center of the page.
The original build survives alongside its artwork. These screenshots were captured from that recovered build, including the original portfolio layout.
A later 2023 snapshot keeps the same lineage while changing the introduction to web and mobile consulting. Both editions are shown here as a record of how the site evolved.
dateNote: The portfolio repository starts on 9 May 2018; its animation and responsive-layout commits continue into July. The later snapshot is dated November 2023.
gallery: Client-work layout from the recovered 2018 build.
The later web and mobile consulting edition, preserved in a November 2023 snapshot.

title: IndiaSmile
summary: COVID-19 information alongside ways to help people through isolation.
paragraphs: IndiaSmile combined pandemic statistics with a community and resources for staying informed. Its purpose extended from tracking numbers to finding ways to stay connected during lockdown.
The original portfolio describes a WhatsApp and Telegram community of more than 2,500 members and the challenge of adapting the backend as traffic grew.
dateNote: June 2020 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.

title: Nataco
summary: A design studio with an illustrated world of its own.
paragraphs: Nataco’s site brought custom illustration, expressive typography and a playful 3D scene into a design-and-development studio website. Its pages covered web applications, Shopify work and design subscriptions.
The repository starts under the Dyeus name in February 2020. A June 2021 commit renames the site Nataco, giving the archive a clear record of that transition.
The original homepage, service-page artwork and animated hero survive. The film below is the recovered hero animation; the gallery shows the site and its illustration system.
dateNote: First repository commit: 23 February 2020. The Dyeus → Nataco rename is dated 24 June 2021.
gallery: An original illustration from the site’s visual system.
Another surviving illustration from the same collection.
videoCaption: The original Nataco hero animation. Use the player controls to watch or pause.

title: Kevin
summary: An open-source interface for an AI software engineer.
paragraphs: Kevin explores an idea that had been around since the teenage projects: let software take care of the repetitive programming work so that more time goes into the idea itself.
The interface was inspired by Devin and named for Kevin Mitnick.
dateNote: March 2024 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.

title: AI Indians
summary: A directory and leaderboard for India’s AI builders.
paragraphs: AI Indians brings emerging Indian AI startups into one directory, with a leaderboard tracking their growth. It was built to make the people and products easier to discover.
dateNote: June 2024 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.

title: Air
summary: An attempt to make the consequences of air pollution tangible.
paragraphs: Air translates air-quality measurements into visual explanations of their impact. The project combines a calculator with shareable illustrations to help people understand the significance of an AQI reading.
dateNote: November 2024 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.

title: Giga
summary: An AI coding assistant built around understanding a whole codebase.
paragraphs: Giga extends the long-running interest in programming tools into AI-assisted development. Its focus is maintaining codebase context while helping with testing, debugging and integrations.
dateNote: January 2025 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.

title: Trend Analyzer
summary: Turning scattered online discussions into useful research.
paragraphs: The Trend Analyzer gathers discussions and looks for recurring topics, helping writers and builders move from browsing feeds to understanding what people are talking about.
dateNote: January 2025 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.
